stemEn: A picture of a boy with pectus excavatum was provided, consistent with Marfan syndrome. What is the most common associated heart lesion?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار mitral valve prolapse كـmost common associated heart lesion في هذا السؤال. Marfan أيضًا مهم جدًا بسبب aortic root dilatation/dissection، لذلك يجب عدم الخلط بين 'most common lesion' وأخطر complication.
reasoningEn: The source key is mitral valve prolapse among the offered options.
incorrectOptionsAr: Aortic stenosis ليست hallmark لـMarfan؛ الخطر الأهم وعائيًا هو aortic root dilatation/dissection وليس aortic stenosis.
clinicalPearl: Marfan cardiovascular surveillance focuses heavily on the aortic root even when MVP is present.

stemEn: A 13-year-old boy has typical features of Marfan syndrome. What is the mode of inheritance?
explanationAr: Marfan syndrome بسبب FBN1 mutation وينتقل autosomal dominant؛ لذلك C.
reasoningEn: The source correctly identifies Marfan syndrome as autosomal dominant.
incorrectOptionsAr: ليس X-linked ولا autosomal recessive في النمط الكلاسيكي.
clinicalPearl: Variable expression is common in autosomal dominant Marfan syndrome.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026

stemEn: A mutation in the FBN1 (fibrillin-1) gene is associated with which syndrome?
explanationAr: FBN1 encodes fibrillin-1، وpathogenic variants فيه ترتبط بـMarfan syndrome في المصدر.
reasoningEn: FBN1 is the classic gene associated with Marfan syndrome.
incorrectOptionsAr: Homocystinuria وDuchenne muscular dystrophy لهما mechanisms/genes مختلفة.
clinicalPearl: Marfan diagnosis is clinical/genetic and cardiovascular surveillance remains central regardless of genotype.

stemEn: A 13-year-old volleyball player is 170 cm tall, has pectus excavatum and a heart murmur, suggesting Marfan syndrome. Why should he be restricted from contact sports?
explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن vigorous exercise قد يزيد خطر aortic dissection في Marfan syndrome؛ لذلك restriction مرتبط بالaortic risk.
reasoningEn: Aortic disease is the life-threatening exercise-related concern emphasized in the source.
clinicalPearl: Sports advice in Marfan should be individualized to aortic dimensions, valve disease and current cardiology guidance.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026

verification.referenceNotes: Sports restriction thresholds require current guideline verification.

stemEn: A child has the hand feature shown in the provided picture, consistent with Marfan syndrome. Which complication is he at risk for?
explanationAr: إذا كانت الصورة توضح arachnodactyly/Marfan phenotype، فالخطر المهم هو aortic root disease الذي قد ينتهي dissection/rupture؛ المصدر يختار C.
reasoningEn: The Marfan phenotype in the source is linked to risk of aortic rupture.
incorrectOptionsAr: Aortic stenosis وtricuspid regurgitation ليستا الخطر المميز في Marfan.
clinicalPearl: Image-based Marfan questions must include the hand image because the stem otherwise loses its diagnostic clue.

stemEn: A patient presented with recurrent fractures, hearing loss, and blue sclerae. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: Recurrent fractures + hearing loss + blue sclerae هي classic type I collagen/Osteogenesis imperfecta clues في المصدر.
reasoningEn: The triad is classic for osteogenesis imperfecta.
clinicalPearl: OI can mimic non-accidental injury; family history and extra-skeletal features are important.

stemEn: A full-term newborn has blue sclerae and a body-bone X-ray was provided. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: Blue sclerae مع abnormal skeletal imaging تدعم osteogenesis imperfecta في المصدر.
reasoningEn: The source keys the neonatal blue-sclerae and skeletal radiograph presentation as OI.
clinicalPearl: Severe OI can present with prenatal or birth fractures.

stemEn: A 2-year-old girl has had two fractures and was investigated for child abuse. Her mother has poor hearing and tooth decay. There is no family history of short stature. What is the likely cause of the recurrent fractures?
explanationAr: Maternal hearing loss + dental problems مع recurrent fractures في الطفل تدعم inherited collagen disorder/OI أكثر من nutritional deficiency أو abuse في source vignette.
reasoningEn: The family history and extra-skeletal features support osteogenesis imperfecta.
incorrectOptionsAr: Rickets وvitamin C deficiency لا تفسران maternal hearing/dental pattern. Child abuse يجب تقييمه بجدية clinically لكنه ليس مفتاح هذا recall.
clinicalPearl: OI and non-accidental trauma can coexist in the differential; evaluate safety while investigating a bone-fragility disorder.

stemEn: A 2-year-old girl with recurrent fractures and a family history suggestive of osteogenesis imperfecta is being evaluated. What is the best way to establish the diagnosis?
explanationAr: المصدر يذكر molecular analysis، خصوصًا COL1A1/COL1A2، كmainstay لتأكيد OI؛ لذلك DNA testing.
reasoningEn: Molecular testing of OI-associated genes is the diagnostic approach emphasized by the source.
incorrectOptionsAr: Skeletal survey يوضح fracture pattern لكنه لا يثبت molecular diagnosis وحده. Vitamin D يقيّم rickets، وbone biopsy ليست first-line confirmation في source.
clinicalPearl: Genetic testing can confirm OI but clinical/radiographic assessment remains important, especially when abuse is also considered.

stemEn: A 2-month-old infant has left mandibular swelling without fever. Cultures are negative and CT is suggestive of Caffey disease. How should this patient be managed?
explanationAr: Caffey disease (infantile cortical hyperostosis) غالبًا self-limited؛ المصدر يذكر indomethacin كالعلاج الأول وprednisone إذا كان response ضعيفًا.
reasoningEn: The source recommends indomethacin, with prednisone reserved for poor response.
incorrectOptionsAr: Vancomycin لا يناسب cultures negative/noninfectious cortical hyperostosis. Cortisone ليس first choice وفق source order.
clinicalPearl: Mandibular cortical hyperostosis in an infant is a useful clue distinguishing Caffey disease from many other causes of swelling.

stemEn: An infant has a large head, short limbs and neck, and broad forehead, consistent with achondroplasia. What is the most common cause of death in this patient?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار cervicomedullary compression ويذكر ارتباط foramen magnum stenosis بخطر sudden infant death في achondroplasia.
reasoningEn: Cervicomedullary compression is the mortality risk emphasized in the source, particularly in infancy.
incorrectOptionsAr: OSA مهم وشائع لكنه ليس source key لـmost common cause of death. Lumbar stenosis مشكلة متأخرة أكثر.
clinicalPearl: Achondroplasia infants need assessment for foramen magnum stenosis and sleep-disordered breathing.

stemEn: A child presented with the eye redness shown in the picture (telangiectasia). Which of the following could be the cause of this presentation?
explanationAr: الشرح في المصدر يربط الصورة بـAtaxia-telangiectasia، وهو DNA-repair/chromosomal-instability syndrome. لكن option 'chromosomal abnormality' عام جدًا ولا يذكر التشخيص صراحةً، لذلك السؤال ناقص الصياغة ويحتاج الصورة.
reasoningEn: The source explanation identifies ataxia-telangiectasia but the preserved answer choice is only the nonspecific phrase 'chromosomal abnormality'.
clinicalPearl: AT causes progressive ataxia, oculocutaneous telangiectasia, immunodeficiency, elevated AFP and malignancy risk.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Answer option is nonspecific; source explanation describes AT

stemEn: A child has ocular telangiectasia, recurrent infections and siblings with the same disease. Which laboratory finding is expected?
explanationAr: Ataxia-telangiectasia يرتبط elevated AFP مع immunodeficiency؛ لذلك D.
reasoningEn: Elevated serum AFP is a characteristic laboratory feature of ataxia-telangiectasia in the source.
incorrectOptionsAr: Hyperuricemia، hypercalcemia وelevated CK ليست hallmark laboratory clues لهذا syndrome.
clinicalPearl: Elevated AFP plus progressive ataxia and telangiectasia is a strong AT clue.

stemEn: A 10-year-old girl has telangiectasia on the eyes and ear pinnae with frequent nosebleeds. She is a good student and plays soccer. Her sister died from the same problem. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: Telangiectasia + recurrent epistaxis + autosomal familial pattern مع normal neurologic function يدعم hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu) بدل AT.
reasoningEn: Recurrent epistaxis and mucocutaneous telangiectasia with a family history fit hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia in the source.
incorrectOptionsAr: AT يترافق progressive ataxia/immunodeficiency وليس normal athletic function. VWD يسبب bleeding لكنه لا يفسر visible telangiectasias.
clinicalPearl: HHT can involve pulmonary, cerebral and hepatic AVMs in addition to mucocutaneous telangiectasia.
